issues.legal_issue: A validating enactment that retrospectively makes one acquisition procedure govern earlier acquisitions prevents objections based on failure to follow the displaced improvement scheme, while preserving constitutional objections and challenges allowed under the governing acquisition law.
material_facts: The land acquisitions had been undertaken under the general land-acquisition law for purposes connected with the improvement, expansion, or development of a city.
A later validating enactment deemed the earlier acquisitions and related proceedings valid notwithstanding the improvement law and other laws or court orders.
The enactment also preserved challenges under the applicable land-acquisition laws and their rules.
issues.conclusion: Objections based on non-observance of the improvement law had to fail. The broad words barring challenges did not exclude objections based on the Constitution or fundamental rights, or challenges permitted under the land-acquisition laws and rules.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(1)(a) of the Bangalore Acquisition of Lands (Validation) Act, 1962, validated covered acquisitions notwithstanding the City of Bangalore Improvement Act and other laws, judgments, decrees, or orders. Section 2(2) preserved challenges under the Mysore Land Acquisition Act, 1894, the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, and their rules. The words barring challenges on any other ground were read down so that constitutional and fundamental-rights objections remained available.

predicates.covered_acquisition_validation_case: The proceeding challenges an earlier land acquisition of the kind addressed by a later enactment that validates acquisitions and related steps.
predicates.validation_law_displaces_improvement_pro: The legislature made the earlier acquisitions valid notwithstanding a separate improvement scheme and provided for them to be governed by the acquisition procedure that had been used.

issues.definition: When a covered acquisition is made valid notwithstanding a separate improvement scheme, an objection based only on failure to follow that scheme fails.

issues.legal_issue: A legislature with authority over acquisition may retrospectively remove discrimination caused by the availability of competing procedures by making the procedure previously followed the only applicable procedure.
material_facts: Two laws provided different procedures for acquiring land for public purposes, and the procedure used for the acquisitions was shorter and more prejudicial to owners.
The legislature later enacted a law that retrospectively made the acquisitions subject to the procedure that had been followed, excluding the competing procedure.
The legislature had authority over the subject of acquisition, and the validating enactment received the required presidential assent.
issues.conclusion: The legislature could retrospectively remove the procedural discrimination by putting the competing procedure out of action and leaving only the procedure that had been followed; the validating enactment was not invalid on that ground.
issues.legal_principle: Within its constitutional jurisdiction, the legislature may retrospectively make one of two competing procedures the only applicable procedure, thereby removing discrimination arising from the earlier selection between them. The Court applied Piara Dusadh v. King Emperor, [1944] F.C.R. 61. The Court noted that the required presidential assent had been obtained.

rule.if: retrospective_validation_case and legislature_has_acquisition_authority and competing_procedure_removed_retroactively and required_assent_obtained

predicates.retrospective_validation_case: The proceeding challenges a law that retrospectively validates earlier land-acquisition actions.
predicates.legislature_has_acquisition_authority: The legislature enacting the validation law has authority over the subject of land acquisition.
predicates.competing_procedure_removed_retroactivel: The legislature retrospectively removes one of two competing procedures and leaves the procedure previously used as the applicable one.
predicates.required_assent_obtained: The validation law received the assent required for its enactment.

issues.definition: In a challenge to retrospective validation, where the legislature has acquisition authority, removes the competing procedure retrospectively, and obtains required assent, the resulting procedural discrimination is cured.

issues.legal_issue: A general acquisition law does not have to yield to an earlier special improvement law when a later validating enactment puts the improvement law out of consideration for the covered acquisitions.
material_facts: The respondents argued that the general acquisition laws had to give way to a special improvement law that prescribed its own acquisition procedure.
The validating enactment applied notwithstanding the improvement law and made the covered acquisitions subject to the acquisition law under which they had been undertaken.
issues.conclusion: The general-versus-special-law objection failed because, after the validating enactment, there was no improvement law to apply to the covered acquisitions.
issues.legal_principle: The non-obstante provision and operative effect of the Bangalore Acquisition of Lands (Validation) Act, 1962, displaced the City of Bangalore Improvement Act for the covered acquisitions, so the suggested priority of a special law over a general law did not arise.

predicates.covered_acquisition_validation_case: The proceeding concerns an earlier acquisition covered by a later enactment that validates acquisitions undertaken under an acquisition procedure.
predicates.validation_law_makes_improvement_scheme_: The later enactment applies notwithstanding a separate improvement scheme and makes that scheme inapplicable to the covered acquisitions.

issues.definition: For a covered acquisition, if a later validating law makes the separate improvement scheme inapplicable, that scheme does not control the acquisition.

issues.legal_issue: A validating law may permissibly distinguish between cases needing validation and cases not needing validation, and the legislature may validate procedural defects within its authority.
material_facts: The validating enactment applied to acquisitions and related steps that had been undertaken under one procedure without following a competing improvement procedure.
Other cases did not require that validation because the relevant procedure had been followed.
The legislature acted within its authority over acquisition.
issues.conclusion: The distinction between cases requiring validation and those not requiring it was permissible, and the legislature was competent to validate procedural defects.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that validating enactments necessarily produce a distinction between cases in which validation is needed and cases in which it is not. Such class legislation is permissible, and a legislature acting within its jurisdiction may validate procedural defects.

predicates.validation_law_case: The proceeding challenges a law enacted to validate earlier governmental actions.
predicates.procedural_defect_requires_validation: Some earlier cases contain a procedural defect requiring the legislature's validating action, while other cases do not.
predicates.legislature_has_authority_over_the_subje: The legislature enacting the validation law has authority over the subject to which the validated actions relate.

issues.definition: A validating law may distinguish between cases requiring validation and those not requiring it when the legislature has authority over the subject.

issues.legal_issue: An estoppel ground raised in a petition but not decided by the High Court must be remitted for the High Court to consider.
material_facts: One petitioner asserted estoppel based on expenditure incurred in laying out land and payment accepted by the improvement board for its sanction.
The High Court had not decided that estoppel ground.
issues.conclusion: The petition raising estoppel was remanded to the High Court for consideration of that ground.
issues.legal_principle: The Court left the estoppel issue for the High Court because it had not been decided there; the judgment states no further substantive rule on estoppel.

predicates.appeal_from_writ_petition: The proceeding is an appeal concerning a writ petition in which a ground was raised.
predicates.estoppel_ground_was_raised: A petitioner asserted that the opposing side was estopped based on conduct or expenditure relating to the land.
predicates.high_court_did_not_decide_estoppel_groun: The High Court did not determine the estoppel ground raised in the petition.

issues.definition: When an estoppel ground was raised in a writ petition but the High Court did not decide it, the ground is remitted for consideration.
